items.title: Roswell Rudd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: Ives published his own music, Ruggles got a few pieces out there

ctx.x: I was a freedom rider quite a bit in the ‘60s, I mean I would tell my employer that I would have to go out and march and protest, and he understood. And so I would go up to Harlem, get on a bus and go down to D.C. and further down than that and try, within two or three days to make some kind of contribution, but mainly to try to talk to other people in this and try to get a clearer picture of what was going on. And I don’t — I would have to say that yes there was protest, yes there was frustration, yes there was…

where I connect into the civil rights, as an artist more than as a white person trying to be in a black person’s moccasins or something like this. I’m an artist trying to be in another artist’s moccasins. And when we’re artists, we’re all wearing the set of moccasins in a sense, okay? And that’s how I felt then, and I think my friend Archie Shepp, who everybody said was very militant, controversial and angry and so forth and everything else, whenever I had this discussion with him he’d just say we’re both artists…
Do you think it takes a country a certain number of centuries to get to that place where the arts have more of a — I mean America is not an old country when we compare us to European countries.
